=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md:Step 5, project-base check sentence: "naming the check and the paths it lists" | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The project-base check guidance assumes paths are always available, although a failed fetch may provide only the fetch error line.
  WHY: A session following the guidance literally may post a less informative blocker comment when the sync produced no paths.
- .claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md:Line 46 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The conflict notification hardcodes `<default>` instead of using `<source>` for the project branch or PR-base merge conflict.
  WHY: A session running `/fix-claude-pr` with such a conflict may send a PushNotification naming the wrong branch.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:Lines 182-189 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The `.claude/` copy lacks review-round-1 sync-procedure fixes present in the `workflow-templates/` twin, including both-drift handling, non-zero-exit routing, and explicit project-branch wording.
  WHY: A session checking out the branch would run the stale sync procedure without base-drift routing, both-drift recording, and the explicit project-branch sequence, exactly the #5260 defect.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:Step 3, "Any other base" case | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The instructions do not specify how to record remaining default-branch guard drift when both default-drift and base-drift checks exit non-zero for a PR head on a non-default base.
  WHY: Merging only origin/<base> can leave default-branch guard changes absent without recording a claude_assets=stale note, leaving the operator unaware that the environment is inconsistent.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:Step 3, project-branch case | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The instruction "sync the project branch first exactly as step 2 does" is ambiguous and does not spell out the checkout, merge, push, and return-to-PR-head sequence.
  WHY: An agent on the PR head may run step 2's diffs instead of updating the project branch, causing verification to fail and potentially entering a blocker loop.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:Step 2, "Both exit 0 → nothing to do." | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: Step 2 does not explicitly direct the agent to proceed to step 3 when either check exits non-zero.
  WHY: An agent reading step 2 in isolation could interpret “Both exit 0 → nothing to do.” as a terminal condition and stop before executing the merge logic in step 3.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:Step 3, blocker-evidence diff | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The blocker-evidence diff assumes origin/<project branch> was fetched successfully.
  WHY: If the fetch fails, the diff fails instead of listing the diverging paths, leaving the operator without structured evidence.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md and fix-claude-pr.md:implement-plan-claude.md:181, 183, 188; fix-claude-pr.md:46 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The commands use inconsistent placeholder names, `<base>` and `<base ref>`, for the same PR-base-ref concept.
  WHY: While not a runtime defect in either command, copying prose between files can leave a placeholder that references a nonexistent remote ref, leading to check failures.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:Step 3, project-branch case ("sync the project branch first, as the procedure's step 2 (**Sync the project branch**) does") | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The text references "the procedure's step 2 (**Sync the project branch**)" but no step with that title exists in the Claude-asset sync procedure.
  WHY: An agent following this instruction will look for a step titled "Sync the project branch" and fail to find it, causing confusion about which procedure to follow. The test `test_sync_only_merges_into_branches_that_land_in_the_default_branch` enforces this incorrect text with `assert "sync the project branch first, as the procedure's step 2 (**Sync the project branch**) does" in section`.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: PR description states "A `hold` claim is posted on this PR until the sync lands" and the twin-sync blocker lists the two `.claude/commands/` files with their sha256 hashes. The PR description checklist says "With the two twins copied over `.claude/commands/` in a scratch copy" tests pass, and "on the branch as pushed only the `.claude/commands` parametrizations and the twin-parity checks fail, as expected until the sync."
  expected_change_site: `.claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md` and `.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md`
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  EVIDENCE: The `.claude/commands/` copies at the PR head ec6ff5c contain the pre-review-round-1 text (no both-drift handling, no "Up to two checks", no source-based conflict notification, old project-branch wording). The `workflow-templates/` twins contain all review-round-1 fixes. The PR description explicitly states this gap exists and blocks the project.
- requirement: "step 4: `<source>` also covers the PR's base" (as documented in the implementation plan).
  expected_change_site: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md:46 (conflict PushNotification template and the byte-identical twin).
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: The PR diff updates step 4 of implement-plan-claude.md:191 to broaden `<source>` to the default branch, the project branch, or the PR's base, but fix-claude-pr.md:46 still hardcodes `<default>` in the conflict notification template instead of using `<source>`.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md:Step 5, project-base check sentence: "naming the check and the paths it lists" | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When the project-base check fails because of a failed fetch (`git fetch origin <project branch>`), the sync procedure names "the failed fetch and its error line instead of paths" (per implement-plan-claude.md step 3). The fixer text says "naming the check and the paths it lists", which implies paths are always available. A session following the fixer text literally and seeing no paths from the sync's blocker might not know what to name in the comment.
  WHY: The session would still stop with a hold claim, but the blocker comment could be less informative because the guidance says to name paths but the sync produced an error line instead.
- .claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md:Line 46, conflict notification: ".claude/ conflict with <default> — decision needed" | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `.claude/` copy still hardcodes `<default>` instead of using `<source>` as the `workflow-templates` twin does. The twin-sync is pending per the PR description.
  WHY: If a session checks out this branch and runs `/fix-claude-pr` with a project-branch or PR-base merge conflict, the PushNotification names the wrong branch.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:Lines 182-189, the Claude-asset sync steps 2-3 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `.claude/` copy lacks all review-round-1 fixes present in the `workflow-templates/` twin: step 2 says "Two checks" (should be "Up to two checks"), lacks "any non-zero exit → step 3" routing, uses "sync the project branch first exactly as step 2 does" (should name "the procedure's step 2"), and the "Any other base" case lacks both-drift handling with default-check re-run.
  WHY: A session checking out the branch would run the stale sync procedure without base-drift routing, both-drift recording, and the explicit project-branch sequence, exactly the #5260 defect.
- Requirement: PR description states "A `hold` claim is posted on this PR until the sync lands" and the twin-sync blocker lists the two `.claude/commands/` files with their sha256 hashes. The PR description checklist says "With the two twins copied over `.claude/commands/` in a scratch copy" tests pass, and "on the branch as pushed only the `.claude/commands` parametrizations and the twin-parity checks fail, as expected until the sync."
  Expected change site: `.claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md` and `.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md` updated byte-identical to their `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/` counterparts via `[claude-twin-sync]`.
  Evidence of absence: The `.claude/commands/` copies at the PR head ec6ff5c contain the pre-review-round-1 text (no both-drift handling, no "Up to two checks", no source-based conflict notification, old project-branch wording). The `workflow-templates/` twins contain all review-round-1 fixes. The PR description explicitly states this gap exists and blocks the project.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
